chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Bukhtari from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

The 'Inn (impotent husband) is granted a delay of one year from the day his wife files a case against him; if he is cured (consummates), otherwise they are separated. If she agrees to stay with him and then seeks the option of separation after that, the option has fallen and she has no option.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations, although they are general regarding the 'Inn being delayed for a year, are predicated on the assumption that he had not entered with her at all. As for if he entered with her, even once, and then impotence occurred to him, she does not have an option against him.

key_terms.تُرَافِعُهُ: She files a case against him

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a husband with impotence (Inn) and his wife's right to separation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the jurisprudential distinction regarding the 'Inn (impotent husband), establishing a one-year period of waiting for potential cure before separation. Crucially, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Furat notes that if consummation has already occurred, the wife loses the right of *khiyar* (option) to separate solely due to subsequent impotence, a nuance that refines the general application of the waiting period.
